q1_issues.issue: The relational-generic trigger fires on 'Trees use photosynthesis' (bare plural subject, bare mass object - both bare kind-denoting NPs), for which the instruction set prescribes the opaque kind relation (Use tree photosynthesis) at 0.9/0.9, not the per-instance distributing rule the parse emits.

carbon_dioxide is a fused modifier_noun compound but carries no genus atom; the compound-kind genus (Inheritance carbon_dioxide dioxide) is specified as always emitted (only the noun modifier 'carbon' is correctly withheld).

'into sugars' mints a free-standing product entity (sk_sugar $x) as the Result filler, with no Experiencer tying a result state to a changed object and no flat copular atom, whereas the change-of-kind/state-result shape reifies the result on the changed object's own symbol and explicitly forbids a separate entity.

q2_gaps: a bare relational generic that carries further modifiers (here a purpose infinitive): an opaque kind relation has no event witness to anchor the (To <main> <purpose>) atom, so the kind-relation form and the purpose-connective form cannot both be satisfied

many-to-one material transformation 'turn A, B and C into D': the change-of-kind shape reifies the result state on the changed object's own symbol, which is undefined when several distinct objects yield one new substance

collective/aggregate reading of a COORDINATED OBJECT (ingredients combined into one product): coordination is distributive by default, which would be false here (sunlight alone does not become sugar), and the collective one-event form is defined only for multiple Agent atoms, so the three stacked Patient atoms have no licence either way
notes: The rule form and TVs, Theme on 'use', the purpose head To with the main action first, the tenseless embedded event, and the Skolem-function terms are all correct; the defects are the generic routing and the result / compound shapes.
